jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Environmental Specialist

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Environmental Specialist for our
Lab & Onsite Support Services (Lab/OSS)
team. As an Environmental Specialist, you will support our clients on-site by managing their hazardous waste programs & projects, utilizing state & federal regulations.  
Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compliance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.    
This position reports to the Operations Manager. This role is based on site at client locations Los Angeles & Greater Los Angeles area. 
We invite you to watch this video to discover more about the exciting responsibilities of an Environmental Specialist at Triumvirate Environmental.
CLICK HERE

Responsibilities:

Develop an understanding of OSHA regulations as well as Triumvirate’s Health and Safety practices 
Preparation of chemical and biological waste for shipment and disposal, including creation of all federal/state waste documents and managing the paperwork for the material. 
Safe handling of hazardous waste containers on client sites, as well as loading/unloading of waste from vehicles 
Conduct safety equipment and hazardous waste inspections. 
Occasionally perform and document Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) audits for clients. 
Deliver Exceptional Customer Service: Champion our commitment to the WOW! by providing outstanding support and innovative solutions to our clients 
Develop a high-level of state and federal regulatory expertise ensuring our client’s compliance needs are met (e.g RCRA, DOT, and OSHA) 
Conduct spill response measures, including the assessment of the spills and cleanup efforts 
Rotating on-call responsibilities as part of our Emergency Response team (optional)

Basic Requirements
:  
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in the hazardous-waste industry, or relevant military experience 
Ability to work as a member of a team as well as individually 
Must demonstrate strong verbal and written communication abilities to effectively interact with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders, ensuring clear and professional exchanges of information 
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues, develop solutions, and implement strategies to achieve positive outcomes 
Skilled in building strong, positive relationships with clients and colleagues 
Ability to work overtime on a regular basis 
Must be willing to work flexible hours within the work week (Monday through Friday) 
Ability to complete a 2 to 3 year professional advancement program in hazardous waste management 
The Environmental Specialist frequently handles hazardous chemicals and biological waste and is responsible for putting on and taking off personal protective equipment. This role is considered safety-sensitive 
Must be able to report to Santa Fe Springs office within 1 hour during Emergency Response rotating shifts if opting into Emergency Response responsibilities 
Valid US driver’s license 
Must have a reliable form of transportation 
Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC) 
Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment 
Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship 
Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis 

Preferred Requirements:

Prior relevant industry experience 
Prior successful experience in a customer service role 
Active HAZWOPER 24 or 40 hour certification 
Willingness to obtain Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) 
Willing to travel to support other regions

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!    
To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on LinkedIn, Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our website !   
Triumvirate Environmental is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE), Triumvirate does not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans are encouraged to apply.  
If you have a disability and need accommodation during the application and hiring process, please contact us at https://www.triumvirate.com/contact or call us at 888-834-9697.  The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. jobs.title: Environmental Program Leader – Hazardous Waste and Dangerous Goods Compliance
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

The Environmental Program Leader – Hazardous Waste and Dangerous Goods Compliance will provide enterprise leadership, technical expertise, and continuous improvement across hazardous waste management and dangerous goods/hazmat transportation. In this highly visible role, the successful candidate will shape strategy, influence enterprise standards, and partner across sites and functions to strengthen compliance, standardize processes, improve environmental performance, and enable safe, reliable operations across the business.

This role is ideal for a senior environmental leader who brings deep technical expertise, sound business judgment, and the ability to drive impact across a complex, matrixed organization – translating complex regulatory requirements into clear, practical, and scalable processes that support both compliance excellence and operational execution.

Success in this role requires a demonstrated ability to work across functional teams to achieve environmental and compliance objectives; strong problem-solving, project management, planning, organizational, time management, and analytical skills; and strong communication skills, including the ability to translate technical environmental risks and requirements for non-technical audiences and influence positive behavioral change.

This position will require up to 30% travel.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities:

Lead enterprise direction for hazardous waste and dangerous goods compliance, including development and execution of short- and long-term goals and objectives for the EHS function.
Develop, maintain, and continuously improve enterprise standard work for waste characterization, container management, labeling, storage, inspection, manifesting, and vendor qualification.
Provide technical environmental support, practical guidance, and compliance solutions to GE Aerospace sites on hazardous waste and dangerous goods requirements.
Monitor environmental programs for compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, and recommend business-level environmental policies, programs, and improvement initiatives.
Represent GE Aerospace with governmental environmental agencies and trade/professional associations to support regulatory interpretation and compliance alignment.
Track environmental performance metrics and drive actions that improve compliance and operating performance.
Prepare comments on proposed environmental regulations and assess potential business impacts.
Support sites with waste determinations, supporting documentation, analytical methods, and compliance execution.
Participate in internal and external compliance audits and support audit readiness, inspection response, CAPA development, and closure verification for recurring or material findings.
Provide governance for dangerous goods/hazmat transportation, including classification, packaging, marking, labeling, shipping papers, modal requirements, training controls, and shipment readiness reviews.
Review trends from incidents, near misses, shipment errors, permit events, and vendor performance to identify risks and prioritize preventive actions.
Lead practical training and coaching for site EHS operations, with a focus on common failure modes and effective controls.
Partner with site EHS, legal, operations, quality, and logistics teams to interpret requirements and implement practical controls aligned to site processes.
Estimated travel required is about 30%

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
Minimum of 5 years of industry experience in environmental compliance, hazardous waste, dangerous goods, or related EHS disciplines.
Knowledge of laws and regulations applicable to environmental operations in the geographic regions where GE Aerospace operates.
Experience working with complex dangerous goods and hazardous waste regulations.

Desired Characteristics And Experience

15+ years of industry experience
Bachelor's degree in environmental or engineering, an advanced technical degree, and/or Professional Engineer (PE) license
Experience with Hazardous Secondary Materials
Enterprise mindset with the ability to connect regulatory requirements to practical business execution
Ability to simplify complex technical topics into clear expectations and actions
Passion for building capability, strengthening standard work, and driving sustainable results.
Humble: respectful, receptive, agile, eager to learn
Transparent: shares critical information, speaks with candor, contributes constructively
Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed
Leadership ability: strong communicator, decision-maker, collaborative
Problem solver: analytical-minded, challenges existing processes, critical thinker

The base pay range for this position is $157,000 - $210,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 13, 2026.

GE Aerospace offers comprehensive benefits and programs to support your health and, along with programs like HealthAhead, your physical, emotional, financial and social wellbeing. Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants. Other benefits include tuition assistance, adoption assistance, paid parental leave, disability insurance, life insurance, and paid time-off for vacation or illness.

GE Aerospace (General Electric Company or the Company) and its affiliates each sponsor certain employee benefit plans or programs (i.e., is a “Sponsor”). Each Sponsor reserves the right to terminate, amend, suspend, replace or modify its benefit plans and programs at any time and for any reason, in its sole discretion. No individual has a vested right to any benefit under a Sponsor’s welfare benefit plan or program. This document does not create a contract of employment with any individual.

This role will require in-person attendance for New Hire Orientation on Day 1.

Additional Information

GE Aerospace offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Aerospace is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE Aerospace will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable). Employees may also be subject to random and reasonable-suspicion drug and alcohol testing.

jobs.title: Assistant Director of Health, Environmental Health
jobs.description:
Description Of Work

Position Definition:
Provides overall administrative oversight and leadership for the Environmental Health division of the Norwalk Health Department. Develops, implements and evaluates a comprehensive environmental public health program in compliance with local, state and federal codes, ordinances and statutes. The work scope of this position includes administrative and technical operation responsibilities, fiscal duties, supervisory duties, and both field and office work. This position also serves as the Acting Director of Health when needed.

General Duties:
Enforces the Norwalk Housing and Sanitary Codes, the Connecticut Public Health Code and the Connecticut General Statutes. Supervises and coaches inspectors, field, and support personnel (Sanitarians, Health Inspectors, Housing Inspectors, Sealer of Weights and Measures, Administrative Support, etc.), assigns and reviews work, provides support, monitors performance, recognizes achievements and disciplines as necessary. Participates in investigating health problems and hazards by making inspections, following up and negotiating to achieve compliance. Oversees lead program, relocation program and eviction services. Oversees and monitors health department vector control activities and water quality activities. Monitors Environmental Health division policies and procedures, prepares updates as needed and seeks approval to implement changes from the Director of Health. Participates in budget development and monitoring. Prepares statistical and narrative reports. Utilizes computer technology to increase efficiency. Directs and monitors activities for continuous improvement.

Additional Duties:
Works closely with other City departments including Fire, Police, Planning and Zoning, Building and Code Enforcement, Public Works, Recreation and Parks, Fair Housing, and Human Services, and State agencies including Superior Court Housing Section. Maintains rapport with the community and industries which are regulated by environmental public health programs. Participates in community meetings and serves on and provides staffing support to boards, commissions and committees as a Health Department representative. Participates in emergency response and planning activities. Represents the Director in liaison activities with community, municipal and state agencies.

Supervised By:
Receives general supervision from the Director of Health.

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of the principles and practices of environmental sanitation. Knowledge of state and local health codes and ordinances. Knowledge of the structural aspects of buildings (plumbing, electrical wiring, fire hazards, etc.). Ability to interpret and enforce the City Housing Code and other sanitary codes concerning housing. Ability and desire to supervise inspectors and support staff. Ability to utilize information technology. Ability to deal effectively with all those contacted. Ability to provide exceptional customer service. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing. Knowledge of formal quality improvement processes. Knowledge of the health impacts of a changing climate.

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree AND five years of professional experience in a governmental public health organization investigating, assessing, or controlling the effects of environmental issues or hazards on human health.

Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Public Health; Master of Public Health (MPH) degree; and two years of supervisory, management, or coordination experience in a community health organization.

Special Licenses/Certifications AND/OR Supplemental Information

License or Certificate:
Registration as a Registered Sanitarian (RS) or as Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) in the State of Connecticut, certification in food service inspection, and Phase I and Phase II Sub Surface Sewage Disposal. Valid Motor Vehicle Operator’s License.

Note:
The above is illustrative of tasks and responsibilities. It is not meant to be all-inclusive of every task or responsibility.

This position is on-site in Norwalk, CT 06851

NASA Grade 8

The City of Norwalk is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employeer

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Specialist

Location:
Davenport, IA
Pay:
$37.50 per hour
Job Summary

The Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for supporting site-wide safety and environmental compliance across manufacturing and construction operations. This role develops and implements EHS policies, conducts inspections and training, manages incident investigations, and monitors corrective actions to maintain regulatory and certification requirements. The position also supports emergency preparedness, risk assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives while promoting a strong safety culture. The ideal candidate has extensive EHS experience, strong technical knowledge, and the ability to work independently with all levels of an organization.
Job Responsibilities

Conduct daily inspections of construction and operational areas to verify compliance with safety and environmental requirements.
Develop and implement site-specific EHS policies, procedures, and programs.
Conduct employee training, toolbox talks, and safety stand-downs.
Maintain compliance with ISO 14001 environmental management system requirements.
Collect, analyze, and report EHS data for internal and external stakeholders.
Participate in regulatory inspections and third-party certification audits.
Coordinate incident reporting, investigations, and related communications.
Monitor preventive and corrective action progress to ensure timely completion.
Facilitate management of change processes for new equipment, processes, and facility modifications.
Track site safety, health, and environmental objectives and performance targets.
Conduct risk assessments and recommend appropriate risk mitigation measures.
Serve as an emergency coordinator and maintain emergency action plans.
Support large-scale site expansion and construction projects from an EHS perspective.
Promote employee awareness, engagement, and continuous improvement in safety and environmental practices.
Provide technical guidance on OSHA, EPA, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
Use required testing equipment to support EHS monitoring and compliance activities.
Collaborate with employees, supervisors, department leaders, and external stakeholders.
Follow established safety and environmental principles and perform additional related duties as assigned.

Job Requirements

Minimum of 5 years of related experience in an environmental, health, and safety role.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited university.
Technical knowledge of OSHA and EPA regulations.
Experience supporting EHS programs in manufacturing or industrial operations.
Strong understanding of safety and environmental compliance requirements.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Valid driver's license.
Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to listen effectively and communicate technical information clearly.
Strong organizational skills and ability to independently prioritize daily activities.
Ability to make independent judgments regarding technical and safety-related issues.
Ability to work with all levels of an organization, including senior leadership.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.
Must meet ITAR requirements as a U.S. person. This includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, individuals granted asylum, or refugees.
Ability to travel at least 20% of the time.

Preferred Qualifications

Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Construction Health and Safety Technician (CHST), or equivalent certification.
First Aid, CPR, and AED certifications.
OSHA 10-hour or 30-hour training.
Experience developing and delivering EHS training programs.
Experience supporting EHS oversight for large-scale site expansion and construction projects.
Experience with ISO 14001 environmental management systems.
Knowledge of manufacturing operations and processes.
Experience serving as an emergency coordinator or delegated department authority.

jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
At Seaman Corporation, every associate is instrumental to our success. Become a part of our growing team!

Who We Are

At Seaman Corporation, we are dedicated to creating and supplying quality, high-performance fabrics that protect our planet, our people, and our customers. From humble beginnings in 1949 to a multi-million-dollar organization, this family-owned business has grown to be a leading manufacturer in highly durable coated fabrics, supplying products to customers around the globe.

Every Seaman Corporation associate plays a valuable role in our company’s continuous growth. We believe by investing in the right people and resources, we can drive sustainable growth across the entire business.

Seaman Corporation products are composed of proprietary knitted or woven base fabrics and coating formulas to produce high performance roofing systems, geomembrane liners, truck tarps, architectural structures, and much more. We work exclusively with authorized fabricators, designers, consultants, engineers, and installers for quality solutions start to finish.

What We Offer

Company performance bonus in addition to base salary
Professional development opportunities including tuition reimbursement, course training, and networking
A competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, paid time off (PTO), volunteer time off (VTO), and paid holidays
Fun and engaging activities including department outings, holiday parties, and our annual company-wide dinner

Seaman Corporation is seeking an Environmental Specialist to join our Operations team! This position will report to the Environmental Manager in Wooster, OH.

Position Summary

Maintain processes and records that ensure compliance of the Bristol facilities with environmental and regulatory requirements. Coordinate hazardous waste disposal, and compliance with air, water, and stormwater permits. Manage corrective actions for spills. Conduct routine inspections. Serve as primary contact during impromptu agency inspections. Support sustainability initiatives.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Other Duties May Be Assigned.

Ensure hazardous waste is managed in accordance with regulatory requirements and maintain databases. Perform weekly inspections. Manage relationship with hazardous waste vendor.
Perform monthly SPCC/SWPPP inspections and quarterly water sampling.
Ensure all real time data is correctly posted to reports generated for Title V.
Schedule inspections and calibrations of bag houses with outside vendors as required by Title V.
Monitor bag houses and water meters throughout Plants 1 and 2.
Manage plant hazardous communication programs per requirements.
Maintain required Contingency Plans for all Bristol facilities.
Maintain Safety Data Sheet files at each facility.
Collect and maintain data for sustainability and life cycle analysis initiatives.
Schedule, attend, or conduct necessary training for Environmental and Hazardous Waste Training as required.
Communicate significant issues or developments identified during compliance activities and provide recommended process improvements to management.
Develop new approaches to solve problems identified during compliance activities.
Maintain a floor presence to show support for the production team and foster positive working relationships.

Required Qualifications

Vocational degree, technical degree or 3 - 5+ years of experience in a manufacturing, warehouse, or operational environment.
Written and verbal communication skills; ability to explain complex technical actions in plain language.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365, especially with Excel, and Oracle ERP systems (or equivalent).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with chemical handling and preparation.

COMPETENCIES

To perform the job successfully, an individual should be aligned with our company values and demonstrate the following competencies:

Do What’s Right

Safety: Safety is our priority and everyone’s responsibility. If you see something unsafe, you are called to say something.
Customer Focus: We are in business for the customer. Our (internal and external) customers deserve our focus and we can create solutions that solve their needs.
Integrity: Our words and actions reflect our values and we hold respect for all individuals.

Work Together

Collaboration: We must share openly with one another, listen actively, and seek to understand the needs of our colleagues. We will respect diversity and work to find common ground.
Teamwork: We will trust the person and attack the process.

Create Solutions

Entrepreneurism: Act with a spirit of entrepreneurism, challenge the status quo, and find innovative solutions to our obstacles.
Continuous Improvement: Everyone is an advocate for continuous improvement. Be willing to learn something new and accept that failure is a part of the process.
Results: At the end of the day, results are what drive us forward. Hold yourself accountable to remove roadblocks and focus on the outcome over the activity.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:
No

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS:
5%

Seaman Corporation is a drug-free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment.

Description Of Work

Position Definition:
Provides overall administrative oversight and leadership for the Environmental Health division of the Norwalk Health Department. Develops, implements and evaluates a comprehensive environmental public health program in compliance with local, state and federal codes, ordinances and statutes. The work scope of this position includes administrative and technical operation responsibilities, fiscal duties, supervisory duties, and both field and office work. This position also serves as the Acting Director of Health when needed.

General Duties:
Enforces the Norwalk Housing and Sanitary Codes, the Connecticut Public Health Code and the Connecticut General Statutes. Supervises and coaches inspectors, field, and support personnel (Sanitarians, Health Inspectors, Housing Inspectors, Sealer of Weights and Measures, Administrative Support, etc.), assigns and reviews work, provides support, monitors performance, recognizes achievements and disciplines as necessary. Participates in investigating health problems and hazards by making inspections, following up and negotiating to achieve compliance. Oversees lead program, relocation program and eviction services. Oversees and monitors health department vector control activities and water quality activities. Monitors Environmental Health division policies and procedures, prepares updates as needed and seeks approval to implement changes from the Director of Health. Participates in budget development and monitoring. Prepares statistical and narrative reports. Utilizes computer technology to increase efficiency. Directs and monitors activities for continuous improvement.

Additional Duties:
Works closely with other City departments including Fire, Police, Planning and Zoning, Building and Code Enforcement, Public Works, Recreation and Parks, Fair Housing, and Human Services, and State agencies including Superior Court Housing Section. Maintains rapport with the community and industries which are regulated by environmental public health programs. Participates in community meetings and serves on and provides staffing support to boards, commissions and committees as a Health Department representative. Participates in emergency response and planning activities. Represents the Director in liaison activities with community, municipal and state agencies.

Supervised By:
Receives general supervision from the Director of Health.

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of the principles and practices of environmental sanitation. Knowledge of state and local health codes and ordinances. Knowledge of the structural aspects of buildings (plumbing, electrical wiring, fire hazards, etc.). Ability to interpret and enforce the City Housing Code and other sanitary codes concerning housing. Ability and desire to supervise inspectors and support staff. Ability to utilize information technology. Ability to deal effectively with all those contacted. Ability to provide exceptional customer service. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing. Knowledge of formal quality improvement processes. Knowledge of the health impacts of a changing climate.

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree AND five years of professional experience in a governmental public health organization investigating, assessing, or controlling the effects of environmental issues or hazards on human health.

Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Public Health; Master of Public Health (MPH) degree; and two years of supervisory, management, or coordination experience in a community health organization.

Special Licenses/Certifications AND/OR Supplemental Information

License or Certificate:
Registration as a Registered Sanitarian (RS) or as Registered Environmental Health Specialist (REHS) in the State of Connecticut, certification in food service inspection, and Phase I and Phase II Sub Surface Sewage Disposal. Valid Motor Vehicle Operator’s License.

Note:
The above is illustrative of tasks and responsibilities. It is not meant to be all-inclusive of every task or responsibility.

Job Summary

The Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Specialist is responsible for supporting site-wide safety and environmental compliance across manufacturing and construction operations. This role develops and implements EHS policies, conducts inspections and training, manages incident investigations, and monitors corrective actions to maintain regulatory and certification requirements. The position also supports emergency preparedness, risk assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives while promoting a strong safety culture. The ideal candidate has extensive EHS experience, strong technical knowledge, and the ability to work independently with all levels of an organization.
Job Responsibilities

Conduct daily inspections of construction and operational areas to verify compliance with safety and environmental requirements.
Develop and implement site-specific EHS policies, procedures, and programs.
Conduct employee training, toolbox talks, and safety stand-downs.
Maintain compliance with ISO 14001 environmental management system requirements.
Collect, analyze, and report EHS data for internal and external stakeholders.
Participate in regulatory inspections and third-party certification audits.
Coordinate incident reporting, investigations, and related communications.
Monitor preventive and corrective action progress to ensure timely completion.
Facilitate management of change processes for new equipment, processes, and facility modifications.
Track site safety, health, and environmental objectives and performance targets.
Conduct risk assessments and recommend appropriate risk mitigation measures.
Serve as an emergency coordinator and maintain emergency action plans.
Support large-scale site expansion and construction projects from an EHS perspective.
Promote employee awareness, engagement, and continuous improvement in safety and environmental practices.
Provide technical guidance on OSHA, EPA, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
Use required testing equipment to support EHS monitoring and compliance activities.
Collaborate with employees, supervisors, department leaders, and external stakeholders.
Follow established safety and environmental principles and perform additional related duties as assigned.

Minimum of 5 years of related experience in an environmental, health, and safety role.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited university.
Technical knowledge of OSHA and EPA regulations.
Experience supporting EHS programs in manufacturing or industrial operations.
Strong understanding of safety and environmental compliance requirements.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Valid driver's license.
Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to listen effectively and communicate technical information clearly.
Strong organizational skills and ability to independently prioritize daily activities.
Ability to make independent judgments regarding technical and safety-related issues.
Ability to work with all levels of an organization, including senior leadership.

First Aid, CPR, and AED certifications.
OSHA 10-hour or 30-hour training.
Experience developing and delivering EHS training programs.
Experience supporting EHS oversight for large-scale site expansion and construction projects.
Experience with ISO 14001 environmental management systems.
Knowledge of manufacturing operations and processes.
Experience serving as an emergency coordinator or delegated department authority.
